title: Geological hazard surveys along roads using large multimodal models
subtitle: Intelligent geological investigation
shortTitle: Geological hazard surveys along roads using large multimodal models
summary: Geological hazard surveys along roads have accumulated extensive two-dimensional imagery, but organizing hazard characteristics and risk information and obtaining slope geometry still require substantial manual effort. This study introduces large multimodal models into field-image interpretation to extract hazard types, survey indicators, and risk levels step by step, and combines this process with image-based three-dimensional reconstruction to obtain slope geometry. A road-inspection demonstration presents hazard locations and levels along the route, while three-dimensional modeling adds representations of slope surfaces and geometry.

media.alt: Framework for image-based geological hazard surveys
media.label: Figure 1 Framework for image-based geological hazard surveys
media.caption: Field images, background information, and engineering survey fields are processed together to produce structured records of hazard types, supporting evidence, indicators, and levels.

media.alt: Stepwise survey workflow and structured output
media.label: Figure 2 Stepwise survey workflow and structured output
media.caption: The survey workflow identifies hazard types and subtypes, extracts general and specialized fields, and incorporates environmental information. The three-dimensional modeling component links viewpoints through corresponding points in images acquired from multiple positions, reconstructs the slope surface, and extracts geometric information.

media.alt: Demonstration of road inspection and three-dimensional modeling
media.label: Figure 3 Demonstration of road inspection and three-dimensional modeling
media.caption: Images along the route show rock-slope locations and level markers. The multi-position photography schematic illustrates connections between viewpoints, and comparisons of images and models from the same viewpoint present slope morphology and texture.

blocks.text: Large multimodal models organize field images into verifiable survey records, while photogrammetric three-dimensional reconstruction provides additional information on slope morphology and geometry. Together, they support geological hazard surveys along roads and spatial verification.
